### save_plot()

This document displays all the figures I make, but I also want them saved to disk — both as `.png` and `.pdf`. I only need to provide the ggplot object, a filename (without extension), and optionally the width and height of the figure. You will not see saving of figures happening in this HTML output file, because I hid those chunks with `echo: false`.

The figures for my written report contain subfigures spread across multiple scripts. Since I want to assemble these panel figures via R code rather than by hand, `save_plot()` can also optionally save the plot object itself to disk as an .rds file, for a final script to later combine with `patchwork`. Set `figure` to the name the figure should carry in the report (e.g. `"SF1A"`) to trigger this; leave it `NULL` (the default) to just save the `.png`/`.pdf` as normal.

A live ggplot object carries its underlying data along with it — for plots built from large Seurat objects, this can balloon the saved file to gigabytes. To avoid this, `save_plot()` converts the object to a grob (a static, pre-rendered drawing, with no data attached) before saving it as `.rds`. This is controlled by the `grob` argument, and defaults to `TRUE`, since converting a small plot costs nothing but forgetting to convert a large one is expensive. Set `grob = FALSE` only if a later step specifically needs the original, live ggplot object rather than its rendered form.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-05-helper-save-plot
save_plot <- function(p, filename, width = 10, height = 6, 
                      figure = NULL, grob = TRUE) {
  ## Save image on disk as png and pdf
  p_image <- p + theme_quarto() # Add Quarto-specific theme
  file_png <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".png"))
  ggsave(file_png, p_image, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  file_pdf <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(file_pdf, p_image, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  
  ## Save the ggplot object on disk as an rds file 
  if (!is.null(figure)) {
    p_rds <- p + theme_manuscript() # Add manuscript-specific theme
    file_rds <- file.path(dir_man, paste0(figure, ".rds"))
    # Convert the object to a grob if needed
    if (grob) {
      p_rds <- ggplotGrob(p_rds)
    }
    # Save on disk
    saveRDS(p_rds, file_rds)
  }
}
```

### theme_quarto() and theme_manuscript()

I created my own themes to add to figures. `theme_quarto()` is used to add themes to figures as displayed in the Quarto document and saved to disk as `.pdf` or `.rds`. `theme_manuscript()` is used to add themes to figures as they will end up in the manuscript.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-06-helper-themes
theme_quarto <- function(legend_position = "none") {
  theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_blank(),
      legend.position = legend_position
    )
}

theme_manuscript <- function(base_size = 8, legend_position = "none",
                         axis_text_size = 6, tag_text_size = 14) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_blank(),
      legend.position = legend_position,
      axis.text = element_text(size = axis_text_size),
      plot.tag = element_text(
        face = "bold", 
        size = tag_text_size, 
        hjust = 0, vjust = 0
        )
    )
}

```

### variable_feature_selection()

I want to remove sex chromosome genes and mitochondrial genes in the FindVariableFeatures step. This does not remove these genes from all further analysis, but it just prevents these genes from affecting dimensionality reduction and subsequent clustering. As this involves quite a lot of steps, I decided to write a function, instead of running all these lines in a chunk below.

You need to provide the Seurat object and a vector with the sex chromosome genes of your particular seurat object.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-07-helper-variable_feature_selection
variable_feature_selection <- function(seu, sexgenes) {
  # Create a vector of all genes
  genes <- rownames(seu@assays$RNA$counts)
  
  # Create a vector of mitochondrial genes
  mitogenes <- genes[grep("^MT-", genes)]
  
  # Create a new Seurat object with mitochondrial and sex chromosome genes removed
  genes_to_remove <- c(mitogenes, sexgenes)
  genes_boolean <- (genes %in% genes_to_remove)
  gene_selection_counts <- seu@assays$RNA$counts[!genes_boolean, ]
  gene_selection_seu_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = gene_selection_counts)
  gene_selection_seu_obj <- NormalizeData(gene_selection_seu_obj)
  
  # Run variable feature selection on the gene-selected Seurat object
  gene_selection_seu_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(
    gene_selection_seu_obj,
    selection.method = "vst",
    nfeatures = 2000
  )
  # Create a vector of the variable features of the gene-selected Seurat object
  variable_features <- VariableFeatures(gene_selection_seu_obj)
  # Transfer the Variable features from gene_removal_seu_obj to snrna_astros
  VariableFeatures(seu) <- variable_features
  
  # Remove the objects which are no longer needed to save memory
  rm(gene_selection_counts)
  rm(gene_selection_seu_obj)
  
  # Return the seurat object with variable features set
  seu
}
```

# Processing

## Open Seurat and filter

There are some outliers, but there do not seem to be major disturbances in these parameters. As the QC done by \[name\] already contained a lot of filtering and elaborate doublet removal, we can be quite loose with filtering here. Thus, no further filtering will be done.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-07-open-seurat
file_rds <- file.path(dir_data, "seu_shortread_astros_subset.rds")
seu <- readRDS(file_rds)
# Test whether it loaded in correctly
seu
```

Some ugliness in the metadata, I'm fixing it here, in the root.
- In the column pTDP-43 stage, all controls and samples ALS17 and ALS18 are empty. For the controls, that's because they do not have ALS and no pTDP-43 pathology, but samples ALS17 and ALS 18 are empty because they have FUS ALS - which has a different pathology.
- Only one sample has pTDP-43 stage 2, so I lumped it together with 3 - otherwise comparison with stage 2 always looks weird, because it has n = 1.
- The controls have empty strings in the column `primary_site_of_onset`, set these to `"Ctrl"`

```{r}
#| label: chunk-xx-metadata-fix

metadata <- seu@meta.data

# How to fix the metadata of pTDP-43 stage:
metadata <- metadata |>
  mutate(
    pTDP.43.Stage = case_when(
      AnonymousID %in% c("ALS17", "ALS18") ~ "FUS ALS",
      str_detect(AnonymousID, "Ctrl") == TRUE ~ "Ctrl",
      .default = as.character(pTDP.43.Stage)
    ),
    # The Ctrls have "" at primary_site_of_onset. Make this "Ctrl"
    primary_site_of_onset = ifelse(
      str_detect(AnonymousID, "Ctrl") == TRUE,
      "Ctrl",
      primary_site_of_onset
    ),
    pTDP43_lumped = case_when(
      pTDP.43.Stage %in% c("2", "3") ~ "2 & 3",
      .default = as.character(pTDP.43.Stage)
    ),
    # This relevel steps makes the visualizations make more sense
    pTDP43_lumped = fct_relevel(pTDP43_lumped, "Ctrl", "FUS ALS")
  )

seu@meta.data <- metadata
```

## Standard Seurat processing (Normalize, Variable Features, PCA, UMAP, etc.)

I wanted to remove sex chromosome genes and mitochondrial genes in the FindVariableFeatures step and created the helper function variable_feature_selection() to do so. The vector `sexgenes` should be specific for the genes which are and which are not in your Seurat object, so when I wanted to do this, \[name\] shared a text file with me. In hindsight, this was not the most reproducible or neat approach, but it is what I did all those months ago, so I'll use it now as well. For transparancy, this sex_gene.txt file is also in the Git repo under `/data/metainformation/sex_genes.txt`.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-xx-processing
seu <- NormalizeData(seu)

## Variable features -----------------------------------------------------------

# sex_genes.txt stores a list of sex genes in my seurat object 
file_txt <- file.path(dir_data_meta, "sex_genes.txt")
sexgenes <- read_table(file_txt, col_names = FALSE) |> pull(X1)

seu <- variable_feature_selection(seu, sexgenes)

## Further processing ----------------------------------------------------------

seu <- ScaleData(seu, vars.to.regress = "percent.mt")
seu <- RunPCA(seu) # Runs on variable features by default
seu <- RunHarmony(seu, group.by.vars = "AnonymousID")
seu <- RunUMAP(seu, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:dims)
seu <- FindNeighbors(seu, reduction = "harmony", k.param = k, dims = 1:dims)
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-xx-clustering
reductions <- c("pca", "umap")

for (res in resolutions) {
  seu <- FindClusters(
    seu,
    resolution = res,
    cluster.name = paste0("seurat_cluster_res", res),
    algorithm = 4 # 4 = Leiden algorithm
    )
  for (reduction in reductions) {
      p <- DimPlot(
        seu,
        reduction = reduction,
        group.by = paste0("seurat_cluster_res", res),
        label = TRUE
      )  +
        labs(title = paste0("Clusters at resolution", res))
      save_plot(p, paste0("clustering_", reduction, "_res", res))
  }
}
```
